text: map, filter, and reduce replace most hand-written for loops over arrays in modern code. Today covers what each one does on its own, and how naturally they chain together.

map runs a function on every element and returns a new array of the results, the same length as the original — the original array is never changed. Use it whenever you want the same list, but each item transformed.

filter runs a test function on every element and returns a new array containing only the elements where that test returned true. The result can be shorter than the original, or even empty, if nothing passes.

reduce is the one that trips people up first. It walks the array carrying an accumulator forward from one element to the next, returning a single final value. The second argument is the accumulator's starting point.

These three chain naturally: filter down to what matters, map to pull out just the field you need, reduce to a single total — close to what real blockchain code does constantly when summarizing on-chain data.

map transforms, filter selects, reduce collapses to one value, and all three chain together cleanly. Next up: spread and rest operators — two more pieces of syntax you'll see on almost every page of real code.
